Landing.heroLead: Encrypt files, letters and crypto in your browser. Split the key between people you trust. Nobody can open anything early — not us, not any single guardian.
Landing.heroNote: Free on public testnets. Needs a browser wallet such as MetaMask.
Landing.heroAria: A key split into three shares held by three guardians; two of three are enough to open the vault
Landing.stat2Label: Plaintext files or keys on any server
Landing.stat3Label: Guardians rebuild the key; fewer learn nothing
Landing.stat4Label: Of actions recorded as public on-chain events
Landing.howTitle: Four steps, and no one in the middle.

s1.title: Seal
s1.body: Your browser encrypts it with a fresh key. Only scrambled bytes leave your device.

s2.title: Split
s2.body: The key is cut into shares, one locked to each guardian.

s3.title: Prove
s3.body: A beneficiary raises a claim with evidence. Guardians review it themselves.

s4.title: Release
s4.body: Enough approvals and silence from you, and the shares open the file.

Landing.featTitle: One platform for everything you want to pass on.
Landing.featSub: Files, letters and crypto, protected by the same rules, with safeguards that let you undo a mistake.

files.d: Any file, sealed in your browser before upload.

letters.d: A message that appears on screen after release.

crypto.d: Lock POL or any ERC-20. The beneficiary withdraws only after guardians approve.

guardians.d: Each holds one locked share. Replace them any time.

heartbeat.d: One tap cancels any claim raised against you.

challenge.d: A window you set to object before anything is final.

safety.d: A guardian can block a claim; you can pause them all.

timelock.d: Keep an asset sealed until a date you choose.

identity.d: Optional zero-knowledge Aadhaar proofs: one person, one seat, and an over-18 check. Nothing from the Aadhaar leaves the browser.

alerts.d: If someone claims, you are emailed a one-time check-in link at once, texted later if silent, and guardians are warned before time runs out.

audit.d: Every action is a public on-chain event. Filter it, or export a PDF with transaction hashes.

recovery.d: Your key is sealed with your password. Keep a recovery file safe.

Landing.claimsTitle: Every step is visible, and you can stop it.

c2.d: Email with a one-time check-in link, then SMS.

Landing.claimsStop: A check-in cancels the claim at any point before it is final.
Landing.privTitle: What the world can see, and what never leaves you.

p1.b: A pointer to scrambled bytes on IPFS

Landing.rolesEyebrow: Three roles, one address can hold several

owner.p3: Check in, cancel, or freeze at any time

guardian.line: People you trust, none of them alone.
guardian.p1: Review the evidence in their own browser
guardian.p3: Release their share only after finalization

beneficiary.p1: Sees that a file exists, never what it holds
beneficiary.p2: Raises a claim once you have been silent long enough
beneficiary.p3: Decrypts only when guardians have released

q1.a: No. Files are encrypted in your browser before upload, and the key is split so that no server and no single person ever holds it whole.

q2.q: What if I forget my password?
q2.a: Nobody can reset it, by design. Use a recovery file. Your inheritance keeps working either way, because guardians hold their own shares.

q3.a: Only the minimum threshold is needed. If some stay silent, a claim can still finish after your deadline. You can also replace guardians at any time.

q4.q: What if someone lies about my death?
q4.a: Guardians review the evidence, you get a challenge period, and any check-in from you cancels the claim. A guardian can also flag it as fraud.

q5.q: Is it ready for real money?
q5.a: Not yet. It is a working prototype on public testnets and has not been audited. Do not store anything you cannot afford to lose.
